newsitem.title: USA: Merrill's Straszheim sees low profit growth in US.
newsitem.headline: Merrill's Straszheim sees low profit growth in US.

text.p: Operating profits for S&P 500 companies in the U.S. should grow an average 2.5 percent this year, forecast Donald Straszheim, Merrill Lynch and Co Inc chief economist, securities research and economics.

Noting that other analysts are expecting a profit gain of about 17 percent, Straszheim said in a monthly telephone conference call: "We simply believe the economic fundamentals will not support anything like a 17 percent earnings gain.
"It's still a great looking U.S. economy to us. We have moderate growth, low inflation."
"The bottom line on the economy is that we still see growth continuing at a pretty decent pace," he continued. "We're nervous about growth becoming excessive and we'll watch this carefully."
He said he would especially keep an eye on unemployment and average hourly earnings as indicators of an overheating economy.
He warned the markets could get "ugly in a hurry if we see much more evidence of labor market strength."
Straszheim does not expect the Federal Reserve to raise short-term interest rates until the second half of this year.
He expects continued strength of cash flows into equity mutual funds.
He sees inflation at about 3.8 percent globally this year compared to about five percent last year.

He expects the dollar to continue to strengthen against the yen, with the exchange at about 120 yen by the end of this year. He cited a slowly improving Japanese economy, as well as low interest rates and low inflation.
He doesn't expect Europe to go backwards into recession this year, with growth improved in 1997 versus 1996.
"The best economy remains the U.K.," he said. Unemployment is under seven percent and inflation is creeping (up) a little bit."
He forecast that the overall Latin American economy will improve this year compared versus 1996.
